author: reek
body: capture and capture-raw were declared as operations of the Camera effect in Foreword chapter Camera with no handler, so a call died at emit with CDX2040. They are real here, over the isochronous endpoint Works chapter GopUsbCam drives: a frame that arrives is a frame the controller delivered, not a constant. Unlike Location and Sensors, nothing about this chapter is a placeholder.

author: reek
body: They are not in the foreword because reading the camera means resetting a root port, enumerating a device, walking a configuration descriptor and queueing an isochronous TRB, and none of that is a foreword concern. Device.Port and Device.Mmio are grounded here so a caller declares Camera and nothing else, which is the same arrangement Kernel chapter MicInput uses for the microphone.

author: reek
body: A frame is the buffer plus the shape of what is in it, so a caller reads pixels rather than an address, and a failed capture is a value rather than a convention about a sentinel.

author: reek
body: The camera sits on root port 3, which is PORTSC index 2: the slot context turns the zero-based index into the one-based root port number.

author: reek
body: The sequence is the one codex/test/apps/usb-cam-frame proves: connect to the controller, reset the port, open the device, fetch its configuration descriptor, find the streaming interface at the alternate setting that HAS an endpoint, open that endpoint, queue one frame.

author: reek
body: Every step answers cam-no-frame on failure rather than a partly-built frame, because a CamFrame whose cf-ok is True must mean the pixels were delivered. cam-read-frame answers zero for success and a negative for a timeout, and the difference matters: a timeout leaves the buffer holding whatever it held before, which would read as a picture.

author: reek
body: Every call does the whole sequence: reset, enumerate, descriptor, configure, one frame. That is what an effect operation taking no handle forces -- capture's declared shape has nowhere to keep a camera between calls -- and it is honest about the price rather than caching a device behind the caller's back.

author: reek
body: So a caller that wants ONE frame uses capture, and a caller that wants a STREAM does not: it cites Works chapter GopUsbCam, holds the UsbCam itself, and calls cam-read-frame, which reuses the buffer opened once. The effect is the convenient door, not the fast one.

author: reek
body: YUYV packs one luma byte per pixel and shares chroma across a pair. A frame that is not ok answers zero everywhere rather than reading an address it does not own.
